T1_reason: V1 loss removes the patch where visual content would be held; the LGN-extrastriate route drives behaviour without a held state. Why extrastriate cortex cannot hold the state alone is not derived.
T2_reason: V1 loss removes the patch where visual content would be held; the LGN-extrastriate route drives behaviour without a held state. Why extrastriate cortex cannot hold the state alone is not derived.
constraint: After V1 damage, people can locate and discriminate stimuli in the blind field well above chance while saying they see nothing (blindsight).

T1_reason: Attention sets gain on inputs; holding is a separate condition, so attention without awareness is allowed. Not predicted.
T2_reason: Attention sets gain on inputs; holding is a separate condition, so attention without awareness is allowed. Not predicted.
constraint: Attention and awareness can come apart: spatial cues speed responses to stimuli the person does not see.

T1_reason: Each hemisphere's posterior cortex can hold its own state; comparing them needs callosal coupling. Allowed, not predicted.
T2_reason: Each hemisphere's posterior cortex can hold its own state; comparing them needs callosal coupling. Allowed, not predicted.
constraint: Cutting the corpus callosum stops the two hemispheres comparing or jointly reporting stimuli from the two visual half-fields.

T1_reason: T1 says a held state cannot span uncoupled hemispheres, so it predicts two streams. Pinto 2017 (n = 2) argue for one. Contested data, so strained, not contradicted.
T2_reason: T1 says a held state cannot span uncoupled hemispheres, so it predicts two streams. Pinto 2017 (n = 2) argue for one. Contested data, so strained, not contradicted.
constraint: Whether a split brain holds one or two subjects is unresolved: two patients detected and localised stimuli across the whole field with either hand or speech.

T1_reason: T1 restricts the substrate to recurrent thalamocortical sensory-format cortex. That restriction is a stipulation borrowed from IIT/RPT, not derived, so compatible only.
T2_reason: T1 restricts the substrate to recurrent thalamocortical sensory-format cortex. That restriction is a stipulation borrowed from IIT/RPT, not derived, so compatible only.
constraint: The cerebellum holds most of the brain's neurons, yet losing it impairs movement and not, as far as anyone reports, consciousness.

T1_reason: One hemisphere has a full posterior cortex that can hold states. Trivially allowed.
T2_reason: One hemisphere keeps its own anterior-posterior loop. Trivially allowed.
constraint: Adults who had one cerebral hemisphere surgically removed are conscious and hold normal within-hemisphere networks.

T1_reason: Content is set by which posterior patches hold a state; removing a patch removes that content dimension while others still hold. Post hoc; shared with IIT and RPT.
T2_reason: Content is set by which posterior patches hold a state; removing a patch removes that content dimension while others still hold. Post hoc; shared with IIT and RPT.
constraint: Focal lesions in posterior sensory cortex remove specific contents (motion, colour) while leaving consciousness otherwise intact.

T1_reason: Frontal cortex is not in the presence condition, so frontal lesions cannot abolish experience. Post hoc; shared with IIT and RPT.
T2_reason: T2 needs anterior re-entry. It survives large frontal lesions only by assuming the orbitofrontal/cingulate/inferior-frontal loop sites are spared or redundant (an auxiliary).
constraint: Large prefrontal lesions do not abolish consciousness.

T1_reason: T1 must add that left anterior PFC sets the report criterion, not the held state. That is an auxiliary assumption.
T2_reason: Damage to the anterior loop could raise the threshold for holding, and subjective visibility more than objective performance. Allowed, not predicted (one study).
constraint: Left anterior prefrontal lesions raise the masking threshold for subjective visibility more than for objective performance.

T1_reason: Stimulating a posterior patch imposes a pattern that the patch then holds; the content matches the site's tuning. Post hoc.
T2_reason: Allowed if the anterior loop is intact (it is in these patients); T2 adds nothing beyond T1.
constraint: Electrical stimulation of posterior sensory cortex evokes specific experiences matched to the site's tuning (phosphenes at the receptive field; face distortions from fusiform cortex).

T1_reason: Lateral PFC is outside the holding substrate, so its stimulation should seldom change experience. OFC/ACC effects need the auxiliary that affective/interoceptive cortex is also sensory-format cortex.
T2_reason: T2 names OFC, ACC and inferior frontal cortex as the re-entry sites and excludes dorsolateral PFC, so stimulation should change experience there and not laterally. Post hoc: the sites were chosen knowing this result.
constraint: Stimulating lateral prefrontal cortex seldom changes experience; orbitofrontal and anterior cingulate stimulation often does.

T1_reason: All agents except ketamine push cortex into bistability, so OFF-periods cut every run shorter than the hold time. Post hoc: mechanism borrowed from the bistability line (Massimini, Sanchez-Vives).
T2_reason: All agents except ketamine push cortex into bistability, so OFF-periods cut every run shorter than the hold time. Post hoc: mechanism borrowed from the bistability line (Massimini, Sanchez-Vives). plus anterior OFF-periods suffice under T2
constraint: General anaesthetics with different molecular targets (GABA-A agents, volatile agents, NMDA antagonists such as ketamine and xenon) all abolish responsiveness, and for most agents, reported experience.

T1_reason: Layer 5 apical decoupling is a plausible cellular route to failed holding; reduced frontal-to-parietal feedback is allowed but not required.
T2_reason: Reduced frontal-to-parietal feedback across agents is exactly loss of the anterior re-entry T2 requires. Post hoc; this is Mashour/Lee's own reading.
constraint: Anaesthetics with different targets share circuit endpoints: reduced frontal-to-parietal feedback connectivity in humans and decoupling of layer 5 apical dendrites in mice.

T1_reason: Ketamine does not make posterior cortex bistable (wake-like PCI), so states are still held: rich experience. Unresponsiveness is disconnection, which T1 treats as irrelevant to presence. Post hoc; rests on one cohort.
T2_reason: Lee 2013 reports reduced frontal-to-parietal feedback under ketamine too, yet people dream. T2 must assume ketamine spares re-entry at the loop sites, against the only connectivity data in the ledger.
constraint: Anaesthetic-dose ketamine makes people unresponsive, yet they report long vivid dreams afterwards, and their TMS-EEG complexity stays wake-like; propofol and xenon give low complexity and no reports.

T1_reason: Presence needs only holding; memory encoding is a separate downstream process, so connected experience without recall is expected. Post hoc.
T2_reason: Presence needs only holding; memory encoding is a separate downstream process, so connected experience without recall is expected. Post hoc.
constraint: Under intended general anaesthesia some patients follow commands with an isolated forearm, yet recall nothing afterwards.

T1_reason: Within NREM the amount of OFF-free posterior time varies, so some awakenings follow held states and some do not; REM is mostly OFF-free, so more reports. Post hoc.
T2_reason: Allowed, but T2 adds a frontal condition that NREM data were not shown to need.
constraint: People report experiences after awakenings from NREM sleep as well as REM sleep, and report none after a sizeable share of awakenings from either.

T1_reason: Fewer posterior slow waves = more OFF-free time = more held states. Post hoc; shared with IIT.
T2_reason: T2 predicts frontal OFF-periods also block experience. Siclari 2017 found the effect posterior; Siclari 2018 found large steep frontal slow waves with micro-arousals before successful recall, the opposite sign.
constraint: Within both NREM and REM, dream reports follow a local drop in low-frequency EEG power over posterior cortex; high-frequency activity there tracks specific contents.

T1_reason: Content is the held pattern in sensory-format cortex, the same format as waking perception, so wake-trained decoders should transfer. Post hoc.
T2_reason: Allowed; T2's frontal loop is not visible in this result.
constraint: The visual content of sleep-onset imagery can be decoded from fMRI patterns in visual cortex.

T1_reason: T1 makes connection orthogonal to presence, so a dreamer who is selectively connected (hears, answers by eye) is allowed. T1 does not say when connection reopens.
T2_reason: T1 makes connection orthogonal to presence, so a dreamer who is selectively connected (hears, answers by eye) is allowed. T1 does not say when connection reopens.
constraint: Lucid dreamers in verified REM sleep can perceive questions, compute answers and reply with eye signals.

T1_reason: Allowed: behaviour is not part of the presence condition. T1 makes a risky prediction of WHO (prediction P2) but there is no data yet, so not 'explains'.
T2_reason: Allowed; T2 predicts covert awareness only where both posterior and anterior loop sites lack OFF-periods.
constraint: A quarter of behaviourally unresponsive brain-injured patients follow commands in fMRI or EEG imagery tasks (covert awareness / cognitive-motor dissociation).

T1_reason: Arousal (eyes open, sleep-wake cycles) is brainstem-driven; awareness needs held cortical states, which TMS-evoked OFF-periods in UWS prevent (Rosanova 2018: phase-locking ends at 167-188 ms in UWS vs 248 ms in awake controls). Post hoc: the hold time was chosen knowing these numbers.
T2_reason: Arousal (eyes open, sleep-wake cycles) is brainstem-driven; awareness needs held cortical states, which TMS-evoked OFF-periods in UWS prevent (Rosanova 2018: phase-locking ends at 167-188 ms in UWS vs 248 ms in awake controls). Post hoc: the hold time was chosen knowing these numbers.
constraint: Wakefulness and awareness dissociate: patients in the vegetative / unresponsive wakefulness state open their eyes and have sleep-wake cycles without behavioural signs of awareness.

T1_reason: A mask arriving before the hold time rewrites the patch before the target state is held, so the target is never experienced, while early feed-forward processing (priming) runs. A sharp threshold follows from holding being all-or-none. Post hoc; shared with RPT, Herzog, Bachmann.
T2_reason: A mask arriving before the hold time rewrites the patch before the target state is held, so the target is never experienced, while early feed-forward processing (priming) runs. A sharp threshold follows from holding being all-or-none. Post hoc; shared with RPT, Herzog, Bachmann.
constraint: Brief stimuli followed by a mask become invisible below a sharp threshold, while still being processed (e.g. repetition priming).

T1_reason: Unheld processing can be deep or shallow; T1 does not set its depth.
T2_reason: Unheld processing can be deep or shallow; T1 does not set its depth.
constraint: Unseen stimuli can drive high-level (semantic) processing, but many published effects are statistically weak and the size of unconscious processing is contested.

T1_reason: Needs an attention/capacity auxiliary: T1 alone does not say why T2 fails at 200-500 ms but not at lag 1.
T2_reason: Needs an attention/capacity auxiliary: T1 alone does not say why T2 fails at 200-500 ms but not at lag 1.
constraint: A second target in a rapid stream is often missed 200-500 ms after a first (attentional blink); on missed trials early sensory responses remain and late responses collapse.

T1_reason: Unattended input may never drive a held state, or be held and forgotten; T1 allows both.
T2_reason: Unattended input may never drive a held state, or be held and forgotten; T1 allows both.
constraint: People miss salient, unexpected objects and large scene changes when attention is elsewhere (inattentional and change blindness).

T1_reason: T1 sides with 'held content is richer than what is encoded for report', but the overflow reading is contested, so compatible.
T2_reason: T1 sides with 'held content is richer than what is encoded for report', but the overflow reading is contested, so compatible.
constraint: When cued after a brief display, people can report more items than they can report uncued (partial-report advantage).

T1_reason: Visibility reports read the held state through a separate confidence process; dissociation allowed.
T2_reason: Visibility reports read the held state through a separate confidence process; dissociation allowed.
constraint: Subjective visibility and objective performance can dissociate in healthy people (equal accuracy, different visibility).

T1_reason: No late frontal component is needed; the earlier posterior negativity (~200-240 ms) falls inside the hold time. Post hoc; shared with IIT and RPT.
T2_reason: T2's re-entry is not the P3b, so its loss without report is allowed but not predicted.
constraint: The P3b disappears when people see a stimulus but do not have to report it; it tracks report and task relevance, not awareness.

T1_reason: Sustained activity from ~250-300 ms on some trials = the state was held; it predicts later reports. Post hoc; one study (grade C).
T2_reason: Sustained activity from ~250-300 ms on some trials = the state was held; it predicts later reports. Post hoc; one study (grade C).
constraint: Without any task, the same sound gives late sustained activity on some trials and not others from about 250-300 ms, and this predicts later content reports.

T1_reason: Frontal cortex can carry copies of held content without being needed. Allowed.
T2_reason: Frontal patterns that carry awareness without a univariate response fit low-level re-entry. Post hoc.
constraint: In a no-report masking design, frontal univariate responses vanish but whether a stimulus was seen can still be decoded from frontal and posterior patterns.

T1_reason: Frontal fMRI follows report, not percept, because frontal cortex is outside the presence condition. Post hoc.
T2_reason: T2 says re-entry from frontal sites is needed for each held percept. Frässle 2014 saw no frontal activity tied to switches without report. T2 must claim the re-entry is too weak for fMRI.
constraint: In binocular rivalry, frontal fMRI activity relates to reporting switches, not to the switches themselves.

T1_reason: Prefrontal neurons may hold copies of the held content; T1 does not forbid frontal content, only frontal necessity.
T2_reason: Prefrontal content without report is what T2's re-entry predicts. Post hoc.
constraint: Prefrontal neurons in macaques track the content of rivalry switches with no report, enough to decode contents single-trial.

T1_reason: The held state spans the posterior hierarchy; percept-following rising along it is allowed.
T2_reason: The held state spans the posterior hierarchy; percept-following rising along it is allowed.
constraint: In rivalry, the share of neurons following the percept grows along the visual hierarchy, and the dominant percept can be decoded from early visual cortex in humans.

T1_reason: Holding is all-or-none (a state is held for the full hold time or it is not), so near-threshold responses in higher areas should be bimodal. Post hoc.
T2_reason: Holding is all-or-none (a state is held for the full hold time or it is not), so near-threshold responses in higher areas should be bimodal. Post hoc.
constraint: When stimuli hover at threshold, higher-area neurons respond nearly all-or-none to seen versus unseen, and weak signals are lost step by step from visual to frontal cortex.

T1_reason: Seen and unseen diverge when the hold completes (~200-250 ms); a prior speeds settling, so expectation moves it earlier. Post hoc: the hold time was chosen from this range.
T2_reason: Seen and unseen diverge when the hold completes (~200-250 ms); a prior speeds settling, so expectation moves it earlier. Post hoc: the hold time was chosen from this range.
constraint: Seen and unseen stimuli first diverge about 150-300 ms after onset; prior expectation moves this earlier (about 300 ms to about 200 ms) and lowers the threshold.

T1_reason: A content is experienced only once held; inputs arriving before then rewrite it, and the held content is dated to the start of its input. Long postdiction (hundreds of ms) needs the rule that a changing input resets the hold. Post hoc; mechanism shared with Herzog's discrete-perception model.
T2_reason: A content is experienced only once held; inputs arriving before then rewrite it, and the held content is dated to the start of its input. Long postdiction (hundreds of ms) needs the rule that a changing input resets the hold. Post hoc; mechanism shared with Herzog's discrete-perception model.
constraint: What we experience at a moment can be changed by stimuli arriving up to hundreds of ms later (postdiction: flash-lag, cutaneous rabbit, long-lasting feature fusion).

T1_reason: Excitability changes how easily a state is held, so a criterion shift is allowed.
T2_reason: Excitability changes how easily a state is held, so a criterion shift is allowed.
constraint: Ongoing brain state before a stimulus changes whether it is seen: low prestimulus alpha power biases people toward reporting detection.

T1_reason: The local mismatch response is feed-forward; the global rule response needs held states across time. Allowed.
T2_reason: The local mismatch response is feed-forward; the global rule response needs held states across time. Allowed.
constraint: A late global response to violations of a sequence rule needs awareness of the rule, while the early local mismatch response persists in sleep, inattention and coma.

T1_reason: T1 needs uninterrupted activity, not sustained synchrony, and no ignition at offset. Our reading; not checked against COGITATE's duration analyses.
T2_reason: Content in inferior frontal cortex with limited dorsolateral content fits T2's choice of loop sites. Post hoc.
constraint: COGITATE (n = 256): content was found in visual, ventrotemporal and inferior frontal cortex; there was no sustained posterior synchronisation and no general ignition at stimulus offset; prefrontal cortex held limited content.

T1_reason: Bistability is the mechanism that stops holding. T1 was built on this, so post hoc.
T2_reason: Bistability is the mechanism that stops holding. T1 was built on this, so post hoc.
constraint: In NREM sleep, anaesthesia and the unresponsive wakefulness state, cortex becomes bistable: a perturbation triggers an OFF-period and the response stays local or spreads stereotypically.

T1_reason: OFF-periods cut causal chains, so evoked complexity is low exactly when holding fails. Post hoc; inherits PCI's one-consortium evidence.
T2_reason: OFF-periods cut causal chains, so evoked complexity is low exactly when holding fails. Post hoc; inherits PCI's one-consortium evidence.
constraint: A perturbational complexity index separates conscious from unconscious conditions in single people across sleep, anaesthesia and brain injury with one cutoff.

T1_reason: Allowed only if delta in conscious people lacks neuronal OFF-periods (no broadband suppression at troughs). That is prediction P4, untested.
T2_reason: Allowed only if delta in conscious people lacks neuronal OFF-periods (no broadband suppression at troughs). That is prediction P4, untested.
constraint: High-amplitude delta waves usually come with loss of consciousness, but people with Angelman syndrome, some seizures, and some drug states are conscious with prominent delta.

T1_reason: Larger network changes in impairing seizures fit wider cortical silencing; not derived.
T2_reason: Larger network changes in impairing seizures fit wider cortical silencing; not derived.
constraint: Absence seizures abruptly impair consciousness; seizures that impair responses show larger network fMRI and EEG changes than seizures that spare them.

T1_reason: Local OFF-periods remove only the contents held in that patch; the rest still holds, so the animal stays awake with local lapses. Post hoc.
T2_reason: Local OFF-periods remove only the contents held in that patch; the rest still holds, so the animal stays awake with local lapses. Post hoc.
constraint: Parts of an awake brain can go briefly 'offline' with local slow waves while the animal is awake and behaving.

T1_reason: Power and hub activity do not enter the presence condition; reduced alpha with no OFF-periods leaves holding intact. Richer content is not derived.
T2_reason: Power and hub activity do not enter the presence condition; reduced alpha with no OFF-periods leaves holding intact. Richer content is not derived.
constraint: Psychedelics intensify experience while reducing spontaneous oscillatory power (alpha most) and, in fMRI, reducing activity in hub regions.

T1_reason: Higher signal diversity is allowed; T1 says nothing about intensity.
T2_reason: Higher signal diversity is allowed; T1 says nothing about intensity.
constraint: Psychedelic and subanaesthetic ketamine states raise spontaneous signal diversity (Lempel-Ziv complexity) above normal waking.

T1_reason: Brainstem arousal is an enabling condition that keeps cortex out of bistability. Allowed, not derived.
T2_reason: Brainstem arousal is an enabling condition that keeps cortex out of bistability. Allowed, not derived.
constraint: Small lesions in the rostral dorsal pontine tegmentum cause coma.

T1_reason: Same as C47 for paramedian thalamus.
T2_reason: Same as C47 for paramedian thalamus.
constraint: Bilateral paramedian thalamic damage causes impaired arousal or coma-like states.

T1_reason: Central lateral thalamic stimulation removes bistability, so holding returns. Allowed; T1 adds the testable claim that recovery tracks posterior OFF-period loss.
T2_reason: Central lateral thalamic stimulation removes bistability, so holding returns. Allowed; T1 adds the testable claim that recovery tracks posterior OFF-period loss.
constraint: Stimulating central lateral thalamus wakes anaesthetised macaques and restores wake-like cortical activity, with location and frequency specificity.

T1_reason: Nothing in T1 concerns the claustrum.
T2_reason: Nothing in T1 concerns the claustrum.
constraint: Claustrum: stimulation near the left claustrum stopped behaviour and responsiveness in one patient; claustrum lesions in 171 veterans related to how long, not how often, consciousness was lost.

T1_reason: T1's substrate is posterior; it needs the auxiliary that prefrontal acetylcholine acts through arousal nuclei, and that the righting reflex tracks arousal.
T2_reason: Prefrontal (not parietal) cholinergic drive restoring consciousness fits a required anterior site. Post hoc; rats, righting reflex.
constraint: Cholinergic stimulation of rat prefrontal cortex, but not of two parietal sites, reversed sevoflurane anaesthesia while the drug continued.

T1_reason: Early visual activation without holding is allowed; T1 predicts such responses are brief.
T2_reason: Early visual activation without holding is allowed; T1 predicts such responses are brief.
constraint: In extinction after parietal damage, unseen stimuli in the affected field still activate early visual cortex.

T1_reason: Bodily content is held in multisensory cortex; T1 does not explain why synchrony drives the illusion.
T2_reason: Bodily content is held in multisensory cortex; T1 does not explain why synchrony drives the illusion.
constraint: Synchronised visual and touch signals can make people feel a rubber hand or a virtual body as their own and shift where they feel located.

T1_reason: Nothing in T1 predicts zolpidem awakenings.
T2_reason: Nothing in T1 predicts zolpidem awakenings.
constraint: A minority of patients in a vegetative or minimally conscious state transiently improve on zolpidem, a sedative.

T1_reason: T1 requires cortex. If these children are conscious, T1 is wrong; the evidence is behavioural and contested, so strained.
T2_reason: T1 requires cortex. If these children are conscious, T1 is wrong; the evidence is behavioural and contested, so strained.
constraint: Children born without most of the cerebral cortex (hydranencephaly) show emotional and orienting responses that some clinicians read as conscious.

T1_reason: Experience in dying rats is unknown; T1 cannot be scored on it.
T2_reason: Experience in dying rats is unknown; T1 cannot be scored on it.
constraint: In dying rats, a short surge of coherent gamma activity occurs within 30 s of cardiac arrest.

T1_reason: T1 is about sensory-format content; it says nothing firm about felt intention timing.
T2_reason: T1 is about sensory-format content; it says nothing firm about felt intention timing.
constraint: A readiness potential precedes the reported time of deciding to move, but it may reflect accumulating noise rather than a decision.

T1_reason: Microtubules play no role in T1.
T2_reason: Microtubules play no role in T1.
constraint: A microtubule-stabilising drug delayed isoflurane-induced loss of righting in rats by 69 s on average (d = 1.9).
